0|7952d769c29caac4fb51c1f0f0c12434c805b127|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: nVMX: Sync rarely accessed guest fields only when needed
Many guest fields are rarely read (or written) by VMMs
aren't accessed between runs of a nested VMCS.  Delay pulling rarely
accessed guest fields from vmcs02 until they are VMREAD or until vmcs12
is dirtied.  The latter case is necessary because nested VM-Entry will
consume all manner of fields when vmcs12 is dirty
checks.
Note
column2: an alternative to synchronizing all guest fields on VMREAD would

column1: be to read *only* the field being accessed
is expensive and odds are good if one guest field is being accessed then
others will soon follow
column2: or that vmcs12 will be dirtied due to a VMWRITE

column1: (see above).  And the full synchronization results in slightly cleaner
code.
Note
column2: although GUEST_PDPTRs are relevant only for a 32-bit PAE guest

column1: they are accessed quite frequently for said guests
is in flight to optimize away GUEST_PDTPR synchronziation for non-PAE
guests.
Skipping rarely accessed guest fields reduces the latency of a nested
VM-Exit by ~200 cycles.
